Reading guides

Bring your books to Panelune on iPad

Start with books you already own. Choose Wi-Fi Transfer for a copy in Panelune, or link a folder through Files to read files in their existing location.

These steps describe Panelune 1.1.1 on iPad. Menu locations may differ in later versions. Panelune 1.2.0 brings iPhone support and an improved reading experience to iPhone and iPad.

On this page

  1. Choose a route before importing
  2. Prepare complete, supported files
  3. Transfer books from a computer over Wi-Fi
  4. Use Files through Link Folder in 1.1.1
  5. If a book does not appear
  6. What stays local

Choose a route before importing

Wi-Fi Transfer sends files from a computer to Panelune over your local network. The imported copy stays in the app’s local library.

In iPad version 1.1.1, the Files route is Link Folder, not a separate Import Files screen. A linked book remains in the selected folder; keep that folder and its files accessible.

Prepare complete, supported files

For novels, choose a complete EPUB file. For comics, use a PDF or a CBZ/ZIP archive containing supported page images. Keep your original files as a separate backup.

RAR-based CBR is not supported by the current archive reader. Renaming .cbr to .cbz does not convert the archive. DRM-protected, encrypted or damaged files may not open; Panelune does not remove DRM.

Transfer books from a computer over Wi-Fi

  1. Connect the computer and iPad to the same trusted Wi-Fi network. Open Wi-Fi Transfer in Panelune’s sidebar and allow local-network access if prompted.
  2. Wait for the local address to appear. Enter the full address shown in Panelune, including http:// and the port, in the computer’s browser. Do not use a screenshot’s example address.
  3. On the transfer page, select Comics for comic files or Novels for EPUB novels. Choose files, or drop your files into the page. Keep an EPUB intact rather than selecting files from inside it.
  4. Keep Panelune open on the Wi-Fi Transfer screen until transfer and library import finish. Check any failure messages before trying the same file again.
  5. Use Stop Transfer when finished. Open All Comics or All Novels, choose a Series and open a Volume. The imported copy can now be read offline.

Use Files through Link Folder in 1.1.1

  1. In the Files app, place supported books in a folder you intend to keep. Download any cloud-provider files to the iPad before relying on them offline.
  2. Open Link Folder in Panelune’s sidebar. Choose Comics or Novels under Library, then tap Link Folder.
  3. Select the folder in the system Files picker and confirm. Panelune scans its supported books and adds them to the selected library.
  4. After adding files to the folder, use Rescan on the Link Folder screen. If access has been lost, use Reconnect and select the correct folder again.
  5. Open a linked book before leaving your network to confirm it is available. Moving, renaming or deleting source files can make linked books unavailable.

If a book does not appear

  • Address will not open: check both devices are on the same network and local-network permission is enabled for Panelune. Stop and restart transfer, then use the new displayed address. Guest-network isolation or a VPN can prevent local connections.
  • Transfer completed but import failed: check the file format, available storage and the error shown in Panelune. Try one known-good book to distinguish a file problem from a connection problem.
  • Folder has no books: check that it contains supported complete files and that you chose the correct Comics or Novels library. Rescan after adding files.
  • New Series blocked: the free version allows up to 3 Series. More Volumes can still be added to existing Series; Panelune Pro removes the Series limit.

What stays local

Panelune does not require an account or operate a developer-hosted cloud library. Wi-Fi transfer is a local-network operation, not cloud sync. Stop the transfer service when you are done.

Imported copies can be read offline. Linked files depend on their source folder and file provider, which may need network access. Keep a separate backup; a reading library is not a backup service.
